text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Federal government may accept airlines' argument about maintenance costs and allow an increase in domestic air fares by 100 percent, sources say. This is still less than the 200 percent proposed by the operators.
- Gabriel Ajayi, the original lawyer of presidential claimant Moshood Abiola, wins court case over which of Nigeria's top lawyers should represent the detained politician in his treason trial.
- Middle East Airlines aircraft makes emergency landing at Lagos airport because of a hydraulic problem after taking off for Beirut.
- Central bank will within next two weeks release list of 52 banks with approval to take over its retail banking activities, finance industry sources say.

- Raw materials research council identifies 10,000 cottage industries across Nigeria to be assisted under the economic advancement programme in which 4.3 billion naira has been set aside to disburse to small firms this year.
- Electoral commission may have registered about 60.6 million voters for local council polls scheduled for March 15, according to tentative computation of last month's registration.
- Local rights activists worry over composition of an African human rights team visiting Nigeria on Friday for one week to investigate the rights situation in the country.
- State oil firm seeks new partner for its engineering company NETCO following pull-out by U.S. multinational Bechtel.
- R.T. Briscoe Nigeria Plc proposes to double its capital base to 100 million naira.
- Chevron Corp's Escravos gas project which is due to be commissioned in May has reached 91 percent completion.
- Less than four weeks to the deadline for liquidation of distressed banks, three merchant banks owned by the government are already winding down.
